title: Always focus the sending app when a notification toast is clicked
head: 00e3b412e050
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates
decision: publishable pending outer-assistant freshness and posting authorization

leads.summary: The stated Telegram premise is contradicted by its Linux notification client: default ActionInvoked opens the targeted message
leads.consequence: Telegram 7.0.9 connects the D-Bus ActionInvoked signal and routes `default` to notificationActivated, which resolves the target session/chat and calls openNotificationMessage on its chosen window. Its no-raise symptom does not mean it ignores the action; Omarchy explicitly sets Telegram focus_on_activate=false. The new unconditional class match has no information about the selected window, so if Telegram owns multiple windows it can focus a different window from the one selected by the action. The code-path contradiction is confirmed; whether the window focus visibly fights in a given compositor session depends on event timing and was not reproduced. Correct the comment and preserve the action-selected window when supplying explicit focus.
leads.triage: Telegram premise wrong: already in Opus notes; corroboration; published in Details

leads.summary: An app icon is not a window identity; a successful icon match can focus an unrelated window and suppress the app-name fallback
leads.consequence: If the sender's icon identifies another installed application or is shared by multiple apps and a window with a matching class is present, the helper exits 0 for that unrelated window. No second candidate runs. An icon is a themed name, file URL/path, or the desktop file's Icon key, not necessarily an app ID. The old app-name-only path can correctly select the sender in the same fixture, so this is a new regression. Validate a sender identity such as desktop-entry separately and do not accept a bare icon match as proof of the sending window.
leads.triage: icon-first false match: behavioural, sent to Opus (followup-1). No realistic case in 93 desktop entries or shipped senders; Sol example synthetic. Dropped. Follow-up surfaced foot agent case, added to F1

leads.summary: A present desktop-entry hint is ignored for notifications with empty app_name and app_icon
leads.consequence: If a sender supplies a usable desktop-entry identity but empty app_name and app_icon (and Quickshell has no installed Icon to substitute), the changed candidate builder returns without attempting focus, yet the toast is dismissed. This case already failed in the old appName-only fallback, but remains outside the PR's stated always-focus behavior. Pass through the live notification's desktopEntry, or persist a validated desktop identity for restored toasts, with a separate test for empty icon versus empty app_name.
leads.triage: empty app/appIcon drops desktopEntry: pre-existing on base, not a regression; dropped

leads.summary: Two overlapping clicks can skip the later toast's first icon candidate on an earlier helper failure
leads.consequence: Click toast A while its helper is still running, then click toast B (with both icon and app candidates) before A exits unsuccessfully. focusApp overwrites the shared candidates/command but Quickshell does not start the new command while its Process is busy. On A's exit the handler increments B's candidateIndex and sets its command to B's app-name; because B's click left targetRunning true, setting command launches that second candidate immediately. B's icon candidate never runs, so a match available only by B's icon silently fails or B's app name can focus a different window. Queue per-click jobs or guard the exit handler with a generation and launch B's first candidate after A finishes.
leads.triage: overlapping clicks: already Opus F2; corroboration

leads.summary: Overlapping open notification-focus PRs need a real integration of their call paths, not a blind conflict resolution
leads.consequence: Open #12388 passes `ref.desktopEntry` plus `--or-launch` into a one-shot focus helper so clicking a notification from an app closed to tray launches its desktop entry. This PR's retry commands pass only icon/app and omit both flags: keeping the retry function while resolving the conflict loses that launch path. Open #7738 arms a one-second exact-window urgent-event listener after a default action; preserving this PR's unconditional early class focus without coordinating its listener changes that sequencing. Both are diverged (not stacked), and a three-way merge has actual markers in the same click/focus functions. Coordinate a combined implementation, then exercise both features against the combined code.
leads.triage: conflicts with #7738/#12388: already in Opus; corroboration; published in Details

leads.summary: Notification architecture documentation still describes focusing only after no default action
leads.consequence: The shipped explanation says a third-party click falls back to the default action, then to class focusing, and describes chat apps as rarely registering an action. The changed Service.qml:380-399 invokes default and always focuses as well, so the troubleshooting description of when and why the focus helper runs is no longer accurate. Revise that paragraph alongside the code and explain the intentional execArgv early return.
leads.triage: docs stale: already in Opus; published in Details

limits: Runtime effects of the full Hyprland dispatcher and precise interleaving of two Quickshell QProcess executions were not tested on a nested compositor; H3 is traced from upstream v0.3.1 implementation rather than reproduced in a headless QML session. Telegram's v7.0.9 client response to ActionInvoked was traced in source, not live-executed. No live desktop was contacted.

Open PR pairs #7738 and #12388 do not merge without resolving markers; a runnable merged test would require a chosen conflict resolution, so their independently mergeable status against quattro is not evidence of compatibility with #11724.

retro:
# RETRO t2-11724
- Worked: Opus's harness copied the real QML click path into headless Quickshell; that made the reproducers deterministic and public-safe.
- Sol H1 (icon false match) relied on a synthetic sender (Signal with Firefox's icon). A neutral follow-up to Opus disproved realistic cases and surfaced a new real case (foot agent terminals). Routing contested leads to Opus pays off.
- Self-check caught a control that tested a different rule from the Suggested change. Coordinators should make sure the visible suggestion matches a tested control.
- The visible budget measure differs between my local estimate and check-comment (about 10 chars higher). Leave a 20-char margin.
- Pasted reproducers contain `##` headings; demoted to bold inside details so they do not compete with the comment structure. Consider asking reviewers to use bold labels in reproducer files.
- The shared clone (blob:none, no lazy fetch) lacked Service.qml blobs; used Opus's checkout for reads.
